# COIN (Coinbase Global, Inc., NMS): Technical Report as of 2026-11-18

## 1. Data integrity notes

- **Source of truth:** every exact price and indicator figure below comes from `get_verified_market_snapshot` (latest row 2026-11-18). The values returned by `get_indicators` for the 10 EMA, 50 SMA, 200 SMA, RSI, MACD, Bollinger lower band and ATR match the snapshot at the snapshot's rounding, so there is no conflict to flag.
- **VWMA is unverified:** it appears only in the `get_indicators` output (134.07). The snapshot does not list it, so treat that number as unverified.
- **Signal and histogram values:** MACD signal (-12.02), MACD histogram (-2.38), Bollinger middle (141.76) and Bollinger upper (176.04) come from the snapshot only. I did not query them separately.
- **Possible partial bar:** the 2026-11-18 volume (9,398,366) is not rounded like the other rows, which end in "00". That may mean the bar is partial or intraday. I cannot confirm this from the tools. If it is partial, the close, low and every indicator on that row could still change.
- **Not claimed:** I make no claim of historical validation, support/resistance bounces or exact percentage moves except where concrete dates and prices from the tool output support them. Percentages below are plain arithmetic on the verified values.

## 2. Indicator selection (8 queried) and why

| Indicator | Role |
|---|---|
| close_200_sma | Long-term trend benchmark |
| close_50_sma | Medium-term trend and dynamic resistance |
| close_10_ema | Short-term momentum and the first reclaim level |
| macd (signal and histogram from snapshot) | Trend momentum and divergence |
| rsi | Oversold/overbought and divergence check |
| boll_lb (middle and upper from snapshot) | Volatility envelope and band-walk behavior |
| atr | Volatility-based stop and position sizing |
| vwma | Whether volume confirms the trend |

The set avoids redundancy. It has one long-term and one medium-term trend filter, one fast filter, one momentum oscillator, MACD, a volatility envelope, ATR for risk, and a volume-weighted average.

## 3. Price action

**Latest verified row (2026-11-18):** open 115.20, high 115.70, low 109.94, close 110.51, volume 9,398,366.

- **Five consecutive lower closes.** The closes run 136.27 (11/11), 130.67, 127.65, 119.84, 115.02 and 110.51 (11/18). That is about -18.9% from 11/11 to 11/18.
- **Gap-downs on 11/16 and 11/18.** On 11/16 the open (119.31) was well below the prior close (127.65), and on 11/18 the open (115.20) was above the 11/17 close (115.02) but the session sold off all day to close near the low.
- **Larger drawdown.** The close is about 31% below the 10/29 close of 160.59 and about 45% below the 9/21 close of 201.05. The 9/21 high of 208.33 is the highest high in the fetched window.
- **Break on 10/30.** The close fell from 160.59 to 143.54 (about -10.6%) on 20.89M shares, the heaviest volume in the recent weeks. The breakdown has continued since.
- **Gains erased.** The Aug–Sep rally began from a 146.23 close on 8/18 and surged on 8/19–8/21 on 16.96M, 17.57M and 22.74M shares. The 11/18 close of 110.51 is below that pre-rally close.
- **Lowest low in the sample.** The 11/18 low of 109.94 is below every low in the fetched data back to 2026-05-18. Earlier lows such as 141.48 (6/25), 139.18 (6/26), 139.11 (7/31) and 125.38 (11/13) have all been breached. **The fetched data contains no prior price history below ~110 to serve as reference levels.**
- **Failed bounce.** The 11/02 close of 137.83 rose to 151.50 by 11/04 (about +9.9%) and then fell back to 136.82 on 11/05. This shows counter-trend rallies can be sharp, but this one was fully retraced within a day.

## 4. Trend structure (moving averages)

- **Price vs averages (close 110.51):**
  - 10 EMA 127.34: price is about 13.2% below.
  - 50 SMA 166.53: price is about 33.6% below.
  - 200 SMA 172.97: price is about 36.1% below.
- **Direction.** All three are falling over the last 30 days. The 10 EMA fell from 177.70 (10/19) to 127.34. The 50 SMA fell from about 180.3 (10/28) to 166.53. The 200 SMA fell from 182.03 (10/19) to 172.97.
- **Crossover whipsaw.** Within the 30-day window the 50 SMA was below the 200 SMA on 10/19–10/26, above it from 10/27 to 11/05 (176.47 vs 176.43 on 11/05), and below it again from 11/06 (175.35 vs 175.99). Today the gap is 166.53 vs 172.97, about 6.4 points. By the data, a death-cross configuration is in place. The spread is narrow, and both averages lag far behind price.
- **Implication.** Trend filters are unambiguously bearish. Price would need to recover a long way before the 50 SMA or 200 SMA is relevant as resistance. The 10 EMA at 127.34, itself falling about 3.7 points per day over the last two sessions, is the first dynamic resistance.

## 5. Momentum

- **RSI 25.84** is the lowest reading in the 30-day window. It fell from 36.31 (11/11) to 32.43 (11/13), 29.23 (11/16), 27.44 (11/17) and 25.84 (11/18). It has been below 30 on 11/02 (29.70), 11/16 and 11/17, and today.
- **No bullish divergence in the data.** Price is at a new low and RSI is at a new low (25.84 vs 29.70 at the 11/02 low). The MACD line is also at its lowest in the window. Nothing in the output shows momentum diverging positively from price.
- **MACD -14.40 vs signal -12.02, histogram -2.38.** The MACD line is below its signal line and well below zero. It has declined from -1.91 on 10/19 to -14.40, getting more negative in nearly every session. Momentum is still deteriorating, not stabilizing.
- **Caveat.** In strong downtrends RSI can stay below 30 for extended periods. The 11/02 oversold reading was followed by a short bounce and then lower prices, so oversold alone is not a reversal signal.

## 6. Volatility and Bollinger Bands

- **Bands (snapshot):** lower 107.49, middle 141.76, upper 176.04. The bands are very wide (the upper is about 59% above the lower), reflecting the sharp decline.
- **Close vs lower band.** The close of 110.51 is about 2.8% above the lower band, and the intraday low (109.94) did not touch it. Looking back, the closes were 119.84 (11/16, lower band 114.69) and 115.02 (11/17, lower band 110.66), so the close has sat consistently 3–5% above the lower band. This looks like a lower-band walk, not a decisive break below.
- **Lower band falling.** It dropped from 166.12 (10/19) to 107.49. A close below it would be a volatility-expansion signal. It is not a reversal signal by itself.
- **Mean-reversion reference.** The middle band (20 SMA) at 141.76 is about 28% above the close. A countertrend bounce would hit the 10 EMA (127.34) and VWMA (134.07) first.
- **ATR 9.19** is about 8.3% of the close and has eased from 11.06 (11/05) even as price keeps falling. That fits a persistent, orderly decline (the 11/18 high-low range of 5.76 was well below ATR) more than a capitulation-style expansion. This is an inference from the numbers, not a confirmed pattern.

## 7. Volume confirmation

- **VWMA 134.07 (unverified)** is above the 10 EMA (127.34) and well above price, about 17.6% above the close. Heavy-volume sessions at higher prices still carry weight in the average, and recent selling has kept pulling it down from 180.87 (10/19).
- **Volume on the decline.** Recent down days have above-typical volume: 20.89M (10/30), 12.55M (11/05), 11.23M (11/16), 9.25M (11/17) and 9.40M (11/18, possibly partial). Earlier summer sessions were mostly in the 5–10M range, so the selling is happening on elevated volume. That confirms participation behind the downtrend. There is no volume spike indicating exhaustion in the latest sessions.

## 8. Risk and trade-planning considerations

The decision is for another agent. The tools support the following:

- **Bias:** price, all three moving averages, MACD, VWMA and Bollinger structure are bearish. The only counter-evidence is the oversold RSI (25.84) and the proximity to the lower band (107.49).
- **Stop distances:** 1× ATR is about 9.19 points (~8.3% of price), 1.5× about 13.8 and 2× about 18.4. For a hypothetical long from 110.51, a 2× ATR stop would be about 92.1. A noise-level stop inside 1 ATR is likely to be hit given recent daily ranges.
- **Bounce risk:** counter-trend rallies have been abrupt (the +9.9% two-day move on 11/02–11/04), which matters for anyone positioned short.
- **Levels to watch, derived from verified data:**
  - **Downside:** 107.49 (lower Bollinger band) is the nearest reference. There is no prior price structure below ~110 in the fetched data.
  - **Upside:** 127.34 (10 EMA), then 134.07 (VWMA, unverified) and the 11/12–11/13 area (130.67, 127.65 closes), then 141.76 (Bollinger middle), then the 50 SMA at 166.53 and the 200 SMA at 172.97.
- **What would change the picture:**
  - RSI turning back above 30, with price making a higher low.
  - The MACD histogram turning less negative.
  - A close back above the 10 EMA.
  - The 11/18 bar not being revised if it is partial.
